what_happened: Re-derived the rejected general detector's gate numbers (2711 corpus files, 92 flagged, 12 sampled, 0 genuine) directly from specs/archive/358.../progress/phase-4-progress.json and found them matching the dispatch's citation exactly; also found the real live corpus already contains two genuinely line-wrapped CARRIED-UNVERIFIED marks in the wild, giving direct in-repo evidence (not a constructed hypothetical) for why the Phase 1 check must flatten newlines rather than scan line-by-line.

Plan-time re-derivation of the live corpus contradicts the research report's projected flag count of 0 for the recommended mechanism. Measured this session over every specs/ file containing the literal token: the task's own research report yields 13 opening-token occurrences against only 8 complete bracket matches, a shortfall of 5. Under the report's condition 2 (flag a shortfall between opens and complete matches as an unclosed mark) that is 5 spurious advisories on one file, because 9 of its 13 occurrences are MENTIONS of the token (backticked bare token, a grep command literal, a regex literal) rather than marks on a carried figure. Flattening also lets an unclosed mention consume text up to the next closing bracket anywhere later in the file, which can absorb and therefore hide a genuinely malformed mark that follows - a recall failure of the same class that sank the rejected general detector. A candidate fix was measured and works: suppress an occurrence whose token is immediately preceded by a backtick or a backslash, and bound the designator window. With that discriminator every one of the 7 corpus files yields opens == complete and zero empty designators, restoring the projected flag count to 0.

Two authoring-time catches that would otherwise have surfaced at implement time. First, the validator's own Tier Justification measurement check rejected three phase tier claims as fabricated: suite_selection_select aggregates a phase's touched paths, and because context/formats/report-format.md returns the __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel, any phase bundling it with a script that suites do cover makes the union a sentinel, so naming suite basenames is a false claim. The plan was restructured to keep prose phases and code phases unmixed, which made every tier claim honest and took the plan to zero validator warnings. Second, the folded record's phase-3 acceptance text names bash scripts/lint-agent-contracts.sh, which does not exist at that path; the lint lives one directory deeper at scripts/lint/lint-agent-contracts.sh. The final phase names the real path and instructs the implementer to note the correction rather than report a missing gate.
